clue.text: Minister parking by a shop, briefly

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a shop is a store

explanation.surface: A government minister leaves the car beside a shop for a quick errand.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a church minister, a clergyman in charge of a congregation.

clue.text: Spy cheers up having received information

indicators.note: having received means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, cheers
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A spy is cheered up after getting intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TA into AT, which takes in GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is a secret operative, someone working for intelligence services.

clue.text: In RADA, get trained to become an actor

indicators.note: trained means taught and shaped, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: At drama school, get the training to become a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles.

definitions.meaning: to pass on means to transmit a message onwards
a race in which team members hand over a baton in turn

explanation.surface: Handing over the baton in a track race.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay is to pass a message on; a relay is also a team race in athletics.

clue.text: Give up work on Hebridean island, lacking energy at the end

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the island's name
at the end says the missing letter is the final one

parts.note: Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone stops working and moves to a Scottish island, tired out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking energy at the end' drops the last E of TIREE, an Inner Hebridean island, leaving TIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to stop working for good, usually at the end of a career.

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the artist to the wordplay

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece is placed inside the other
new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a brand is a class or kind, as in a brand of humour

explanation.surface: A painter takes a class during the new school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of 'term' into REMT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the great Dutch painter of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Supporter has confidence in team initially put out

indicators.note: put out means removed, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to have confidence in someone is to trust them

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fan backs the team before its first game is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUSTS loses one T, the first letter of 'team'.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a supporting frame or a surgical support for a hernia.

parts.note: to rein is to control, as a rider does a horse
strongarm tactics means the use of force

explanation.surface: Tighten control by using bully-boy methods.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to make stronger by adding support.

parts.note: to get to someone is to annoy them, to gall
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Hurrying to arrive at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get to' looks like arriving; here it means irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallop is to run fast, like a horse at full speed, so to race.

clue.text: Make use of extremely despicable trick

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: a ploy is a trick or ruse

explanation.surface: Employ a thoroughly nasty dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'despicable' but takes its end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy something is to put it into action, bringing it into effective use.

clue.text: Scene of conflict in region harbouring indefinite number

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a region is an area
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A war zone in a region that hides an unknown number of fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of contest, originally where gladiators fought.

clue.text: Story about doctor, American, in big car

indicators.note: about means going around, so the story wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a falsehood
MO is a medical officer, a military doctor

explanation.surface: A tale about an American doctor riding in a large car.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large, luxurious car, often chauffeur-driven.

clue.text: Draw large aquatic creature close to ferry

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes
an otter is a water-loving mammal

indicators.note: close to means the end of the next word, its last letter

explanation.surface: A sketch of a big water animal near a ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb about sketching; it is a noun, a prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw, as a noun, is a raffle in which winners are picked by chance.

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and sorted out, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Things become calm once a state of agitation has been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful means calm and soothing, giving a chance to unwind.

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
seeing is vision, the sense of sight

explanation.surface: A definition of what must be met before one can see.
explanation.definitionFit: A provision is a condition or stipulation in an agreement, something that must be met.

clue.text: Stealing a march on sly type during trip

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: an outing is a trip
a fox is a cunning person

explanation.surface: Getting ahead of a cunning rival while on an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfoxing means outwitting, getting the better of someone by cunning.

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: India is a country
ones are individuals, single units

explanation.surface: People coming into a land in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a republic in south-east Asia made of many islands.

parts.note: difficult means hard

explanation.surface: A tough year for a writer from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy was the English novelist who wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

indicators.note: surrounding means going around, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: heritage is history, what is handed down

explanation.surface: An ancient refuge where a man is enclosed by the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage is a secluded dwelling or retreat, a refuge from the world.

indicators.note: cast in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: bronze as a colour is a tan, a brownish shade

explanation.surface: A huge statue of an Italian cast in bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests metal-founding, but 'cast in' only signals placing one piece inside another; bronze is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, one of the huge gods of Greek myth; a colossus is a giant too.

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
to issue something is to send it out, broadcast it

explanation.surface: A television network's nervy transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Network' suggests TV; it is a mesh of cells in biology.
explanation.definitionFit: A tissue is a mesh of cells or a fine woven fabric, a network in both senses.

parts.note: to discourage is to deter
a fellow is a gent, a man

explanation.surface: Putting off a man who comes to clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' looks like a person but is a substance, a washing agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent such as washing-up liquid.

clue.text: Article put in shelter for occupier

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item placed in a refuge for a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is a person who rents and lives in a property, an occupant.

clue.text: Old Japanese commander holding end of blunt weapon

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a shogun was a hereditary military ruler of feudal Japan

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A samurai-era ruler carrying a weapon with a blunt end.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a firearm firing a spread of pellets, a kind of weapon.

definitions.meaning: new here means inexperienced or raw
a golf course has smooth areas round each hole for putting

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'course' is a golf course, not a meal or a study course.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced, and the green is the putting area on a golf course.

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
borders are edges, or rims

explanation.surface: Dark red edges on the inside of a study room.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a rich, deep shade of red.

parts.note: a monk lives in a cell in a monastery

explanation.surface: An old instrument kept in a monk's bare room.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument played between the knees.

definitions.meaning: to take is to grab hold of, capture
the French word for the number sixteen, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Grab sixteen from a person in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab or capture something is a synonym of take, and the French number sixteen has the same spelling.

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: Surveyors in property generally assess buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' reads as a noun for valuers to assess; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to all, so it is a synonym of general.

clue.text: Most noticeable having dismissed sides from elsewhere

indicators.note: dismissed sides means both outer letters of the word are removed

parts.note: salient means most noticeable, prominent

explanation.surface: The most prominent figure, having sacked his aides, came from another place.
explanation.walkthrough: SALIENT loses its outer letters S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or outsider, something from another place.

clue.text: Programme: a grand finale anticipated, originally

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
a finale is an end

indicators.note: originally means at the start, the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A show's billing: a big finish is expected.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a schedule or programme of business.

clue.text: Key batsman, first to face the bowling

definitions.meaning: a key is a device that unlocks, as a tin or bottle device does

definitions.text: batsman, first to face the bowling
definitions.meaning: in cricket the batsmen who start the innings face the first deliveries

explanation.surface: An important cricket batsman takes the first ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the two batsmen who start an innings face the opening bowlers.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener is any device that opens, like a key, and in cricket a batsman who begins the innings.
